title: AI music, videos featuring Rene Baterbonia flood social media, streaming platforms
summary: Rene Baterbonia's image and story have continued to appear across social media and music-streaming platforms, months after the Ateneo de Manila University basketball player died in a drowning…

blocks.text: Rene Baterbonia's image and story have continued to appear across social media and music-streaming platforms, months after the Ateneo de Manila University basketball player died in a drowning incident.
Among those circulating online are songs dedicated to Rene, with some using AI-generated music and others appearing to be AI covers or altered versions of existing songs.
One example is “Kalapastanganan,” credited to fitterkarma, which has been re-presented as AI covers of various genres and styles.
Other Rene-related releases include “Baon ang Pangarap,” credited to Andrei AI Music and “Tribute for Rene Baterbonia” by Nihvan.
There are also other music uploads carrying Rene’s name or referencing his death, showing how his story has continued to circulate beyond social media and into streaming services.
There are also AI-generated videos featuring Baterbonia in different scenarios, from still playing basketball to rising out of waters to begging for social media interactions.

These digitally created clips have added another form of online remembrance surrounding the late athlete, with his likeness being used to depict moments and activities that did not necessarily occur in real life.

The growing collection of AI-generated and AI-assisted content has effectively created a digital archive of sorts around Rene, combining original tribute material, covers, edited imagery and fabricated video scenes.
Meanwhile, Rene’s mother continues to ask supporters to keep the focus on prayer and the family’s ongoing pursuit of justice.
In a Facebook post on September 5, Rovelyn asked supporters not to hold a large celebration or bring material offerings to her son’s grave for his 90th or 100th day commemoration.
“Gusto ko lang ng simpleng pagdasal,” she wrote, explaining that she wants to prioritize the case involving her son.
Rovelyn also said that people who wish to help the family financially may send voluntary assistance directly to her instead of bringing food, decorations or other material gifts.

She included her e-wallet details in the post and asked donors to provide screenshots of their transactions for verification. The request follows previous statements from Rovelyn concerning financial assistance and the use of her son's name.
Rovelyn has consistently maintained that justice remains her primary concern.
“Hustisya po ang hiling ko di po PERA,” she previously said, while expressing gratitude to those who continued to support the family.
Meanwhile, Ateneo de Manila University said in August that it remained in communication with the Baterbonia family and was willing to meet with them to provide answers and support.
